response: The sub-classification of low-grade cerebellar astrocytoma is not clinically meaningful. Discordant observations due to interobserver variability make histological sub-classification of low-grade cerebellar astrocytomas in children insufficient for predicting prognosis and biological behavior. In fact, similar survival rates have been observed in patients with grades I and II tumors, indicating that tumor grade has no prognostic significance within this group of patients. Instead, "surgically gross-total removal", especially if the tumor is located in the fourth ventricle, is of the highest importance for long-term survival. Therefore, histological sub-classification of the tumors has no predictive value, and treatment decisions should focus on achieving complete surgical removal of the tumor.
